sentences.en: Sabrina Tavernisi described why, for the first time in generations, the birth rate in the United
sentences.zh: 萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西讲述了为什么几代人以来美国出生率首次出现下降，以及这种趋势带来的长期风险。

sentences.en: States has been falling and the long-term risks posed by that trend.
sentences.zh: 其中一个风险是美国

sentences.en: One of those risks is that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 最终可能会走上像日本这样的国家的道路，那里的持续低出生率导致人口逐年萎缩。

sentences.en: could eventually follow the path of a country like Japan, where a persistently low birth rate has resulted in a shrinking population that grows smaller and smaller by the year.
sentences.zh: 今天，我采访了东京分社社长望月崇子，以了解这种变化在日本国内看起来和感觉起来是怎样的。

sentences.en: Today, I turn to Tokyo Bureau Chief Motoko Rich to understand what that change has looked and felt like inside Japan.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月5日，星期三。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, May 5th.
sentences.zh: 崇子，跟我讲讲你造访过的那个小镇吧。

sentences.en: Motoko, tell me about this town that you had visited.
sentences.zh: 这是一个叫名栗的小镇。

sentences.en: So it's a little town called Nagoro.
sentences.zh: 它位于四国岛上，非常偏远。

sentences.en: It's on the island of Shikoku, and it's pretty remote.
sentences.zh: 日本其实不算太大，但去那里似乎花了很长时间。

sentences.en: Japan's not that big of a country, and yet it seemed to take a really long time to get here.
sentences.zh: 我们从东京飞到一个叫高知的中等城市。

sentences.en: We flew from Tokyo to this, you know, medium-sized city called Kochi.
sentences.zh: 然后从那里，我们得坐火车再换乘大巴。

sentences.en: And then from there, we have to take a train and then a bus.
sentences.zh: 很明显，我们正离已知的文明越来越远。

sentences.en: And we're clearly just moving further and further away from known civilization.
sentences.zh: 那里没有便利店，没有加油站。

sentences.en: There are no convenience stores, no gas stations.
sentences.zh: 然后你终于到达了这个偏远的小村庄。

sentences.en: And then you finally get to this little remote village.
sentences.zh: 那里是什么样的？

sentences.en: And what is it like there?
sentences.zh: 感觉有点诡异，因为当你开车进镇时，你已经走过了那些盘山路，文明的迹象一直在消失。

sentences.en: So it's kind of eerie because you're driving into town and you've already been coming up these winding roads and signs of civilization have been disappearing.
sentences.zh: 然后你开始看到这些人形玩偶。

sentences.en: And you start to see these figures.
sentences.zh: 一个栖息在路边的小矮墙上。

sentences.en: One perched on a little wall on the side of the road.
sentences.zh: 田野里好像蹲着一个老妇人。

sentences.en: There's what appears to be an old woman crouched over in a field.
sentences.zh: 看起来好像有个家伙在从树上摇下栗子。

sentences.en: There looks like this guy is kind of shaking chestnuts out of a tree.
sentences.zh: 有几个建筑工人在抽烟休息。

sentences.en: There are a couple of construction workers on a cigarette break.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我不知道，看到这一切让人感到一种深切的悲伤和触动。

sentences.en: And it's really, I don't know, profoundly sort of sad and moving to see all this.
sentences.zh: 当我在镇上走动时，我总感觉眼角余光有人影，我以为他们是真人。

sentences.en: As I walk around town, I keep seeing these people out of the corner of my eye, and I think they're real people.
sentences.zh: 然后你发现，他们的眼睛都是纽扣做的，还有小小的嘴巴。

sentences.en: And you see, just they all have like button eyes, little mouths.
sentences.zh: 它们其实做得非常逼真。

sentences.en: They're actually like quite lifelike.
sentences.zh: 然后你意识到它们全都是玩偶。

sentences.en: And you realize they're all dolls.
sentences.zh: 玩偶。

sentences.en: Dolls.
sentences.zh: 玩偶。

sentences.en: Dolls.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 真人大小的玩偶。

sentences.en: Human-sized dolls.
sentences.zh: 填充玩偶。

sentences.en: Stuffed dolls.
sentences.zh: 填充玩偶。

sentences.en: Stuffed dolls.
sentences.zh: 就像超大的布娃娃。

sentences.en: Like oversized cloth dolls.
sentences.zh: 呃。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 成百上千个这样真人大小的玩偶。

sentences.en: Dozens and dozens and dozens of these life-sized dolls.
sentences.zh: 就像妈妈、爸爸、小孩、小婴儿。

sentences.en: Like a mom, a dad, a kid, a little baby.
sentences.zh: 玩偶。

sentences.en: Dolls.
sentences.zh: 到处都是。

sentences.en: Everywhere.
sentences.zh: 更诡异的是，镇中心有一所学校。

sentences.en: And what's even more eerie is that there's a school in the middle of the town.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它看起来就像一栋大学校建筑，前面有一个很大的碎石操场。

sentences.en: And, you know, it just looks like a big school building with a big gravel yard in front.
sentences.zh: 然后你上楼，有几间教室，你探头进去，里面全是玩偶。

sentences.en: And then you go upstairs, and there are a couple of classrooms, and you peek in, and they're filled with dolls.
sentences.zh: 原来这个村庄只剩下大约二十名成年人，而且没有儿童。

sentences.en: It turns out that this is a village that only has about two dozen adults, and there are no children.
sentences.zh: 有个叫绫野君美的女性，决定用玩偶把这个地方填满。

sentences.en: And there's this woman, Kimi Ayano, who's decided to kind of fill the place with dolls.
sentences.zh: 那么为什么这个镇上的人这么少呢？

sentences.en: So why is it that there are so few people in this town?
sentences.zh: 它怎么基本上变成了一个玩偶小镇？

sentences.en: How is it that it has basically become a town of dolls?
sentences.zh: 基本上，名栗的出生率已经降到了零。

sentences.en: So basically, the birth rate in Nagarou has just fallen to zero.
sentences.zh: 这个镇上完全没有孩子，自从最后两个孩子在2012年从小学毕业后就再也没有了。

sentences.en: There are no children in this town at all, and there haven't been since the last two graduated from elementary school in 2012.
sentences.zh: 那里的大多数人都是老人。

sentences.en: Most of the people there are just old.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是日本其他地区现状的一个缩影。

sentences.en: And that's kind of emblematic of what's going on in the rest of Japan.
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，日本是世界上老龄化最严重的国家。

sentences.en: Japan is technically the grayest country in the world.
sentences.zh: 近30%的人口超过65岁。

sentences.en: Close to 30% of the population is over 65.
sentences.zh: 而且人口在不断减少。

sentences.en: And the population is shrinking.
sentences.zh: 自2007年以来一直在减少。

sentences.en: It's been shrinking since 2007.
sentences.zh: 你面临着大量老年人口的沉重负担，这本身并不是问题，

sentences.en: And you have this overhang of a lot of old people, which in and of itself is not a problem,
sentences.zh: 除非你没有足够的年轻人去工作、去纳税、去养老院工作，这样就失衡了。

sentences.en: except that if you don't have enough young people to work, to pay taxes, to work in the nursing homes, you've got this imbalance.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 日本是怎么走到出生率如此之低这一步的？

sentences.en: And how did Japan get to this stage of having such a low birth rate?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得这是一个很长的故事，你得稍微往前倒溯一下。

sentences.en: Well, I think it's a long story, and you have to kind of back up a little bit.
sentences.zh: 日本从二战的废墟中崛起。

sentences.en: Japan rose from the ashes of World War II.
sentences.zh: 战后，日本决心卷土重来。

sentences.en: So after the war, Japan was determined to come roaring back.
sentences.zh: 凭借人民的勤劳以及管理层与工人之间紧密的纽带，它成长为世界第二大经济体。

sentences.en: It grew into the world's second largest economy, thanks to the diligence of its people and the strong bonds between management and workers.
sentences.zh: 他们做到这一点的方式是通过他们拥有的一种社会契约，主要是针对男性的，

sentences.en: And the way they sort of did that was through this social contract that they had, mainly with men,
sentences.zh: 那就是如果你去一家公司工作，你就要为之奉献一生。

sentences.en: which is that if you went to work for a company, you would devote your life to that.
sentences.zh: 你得早出晚归，按照公司的要求加班加点，成为一名公司职员，作为交换，你将获得终身雇用的保障。

sentences.en: You would work morning, noon, and night, as long hours as demanded by the company, and you'd become the salaryman in an exchange for which you were guaranteed lifetime employment.
sentences.zh: 你知道自己有工作保障，随着年龄增长，你会加薪和晋升，直到退休。

sentences.en: You knew you had job security, you knew you'd get your raises and your promotions as you got older until you retired.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 这就是日本臭名昭著的紧张工作文化的诞生，人们（绝大多数是男性）似乎把工作置于生活的中心。

sentences.en: So this is the birth of Japan's notoriously intense work culture where people, overwhelmingly men, seem to put work at the center of their lives.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，你通常会结婚，并有一个待在家里的妻子，操持家务，照顾家庭，照顾孩子。

sentences.en: And at the same time, you often would get married and you'd have a wife who was at home, tending the home fires, taking care of the house, taking care of the children.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Gotcha.
sentences.zh: 然后在20世纪70年代，就像世界上许多其他地方一样，女性开始进入职场。

sentences.en: And then in the 1970s, as in many other places around the world, women start to enter the workforce.
sentences.zh: 主要是未婚女性，她们工作到结婚为止。

sentences.en: Mostly unmarried women who were working until they got married.
sentences.zh: 但后来有些女性想要工作更长时间。

sentences.en: But then there were some women who wanted to work longer than that.
sentences.zh: 当时经济确实非常好，强劲增长，日本正处于繁荣期。

sentences.en: And then the economy was really doing well and going strong and Japan was booming.
sentences.zh: 随着日本人民全身心投入到金钱游戏中。

sentences.en: As Japanese people devoted themselves to the money game.
sentences.zh: 日本公司在曼哈顿买下房地产，买下全美各地的公司，

sentences.en: Japanese companies were buying up real estate in Manhattan and buying up companies all over America
sentences.zh: 每个人都在写书说我们会被日本吃掉午餐。

sentences.en: and everybody was writing books about how we were going to get our lunch eaten by Japan.
sentences.zh: 房地产和股市飙升，制造了泡沫。

sentences.en: The real estate and stock markets shot up, creating a bubble.
sentences.zh: 然后这一切在90年代初戛然而止。

sentences.en: And then everything came crashing to a halt in the early 90s.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是一段长期的经济停滞期。

sentences.en: And a prolonged period of stagnation set in.
sentences.zh: 这被称为失去的二十年。

sentences.en: It's been called the lost 20 years.
sentences.zh: 所以在那个时候，许多以前拥有那些非常安逸、有保障、终身雇用工作的男性，

sentences.en: So at that point, a lot of men who had previously had all these really cushy, secure, lifelong employment jobs
sentences.zh: 要么被解雇了，要么他们的工资完全停滞不前。

sentences.en: were either thrown out of the jobs or their wages were completely stagnating.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 为了维持家庭生计，越来越多的女性进入了职场。

sentences.en: And so to keep families afloat, more and more women entered the workforce.
sentences.zh: 这对日本的出生率有什么影响？

sentences.en: And what does that do to the birth rate in Japan?
sentences.zh: 所以在那个时候，出生率确实开始下降，因为女性不再仅仅待在家里，

sentences.en: So at that point, the birth rate does start to fall because instead of the women only being at home,
sentences.zh: 她们在工作，帮助国家从这场崩溃中恢复，维持家庭生计。

sentences.en: they're working, helping the country try and recover from this crash, keeping their families afloat.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 起初，人们认为这并不是什么特别的问题。

sentences.en: And at first, I don't think people see this as a particular problem.
sentences.zh: 日本是一个人口非常拥挤的国家。

sentences.en: Japan is a very crowded, populous country.
sentences.zh: 当时新生儿减少，大家似乎并不觉得这是件多大的事。

sentences.en: And fewer people being born at the time, I don't think was seen as such a big deal.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 这被视为一种必要的权衡。

sentences.en: It's kind of seen as a necessary trade-off.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 他们正试图让经济重新站起来。

sentences.en: They're trying to get the economy back on its feet.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 那接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: So then what happens?
sentences.zh: 对日本来说，这是一段相当长的经济停滞期。

sentences.en: So this is a pretty long period of stagnation for Japan.
sentences.zh: 他们很难从这场经济衰退中爬出来。

sentences.en: They're having a really hard time climbing out of this buSt.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，许多男性开始感到非常没有安全感，因为要么他们找不到好工作，要么即使他们拥有被认为还不错的工作，

sentences.en: And during this period, a lot of the men are starting to feel very insecure because either they can't get a good job or even if they have what's considered a decent job,
sentences.zh: 他们的工资也没有上涨。

sentences.en: their wages are not increasing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们觉得，哦，也许我不应该结婚，因为我觉得自己养不起妻子和家庭。

sentences.en: So they're feeling like, ooh, maybe I shouldn't get married because I don't think that I can support a wife and a family.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 这当然导致了出生率的进一步下降。

sentences.en: And that, of course, leads to even more decline in the birth rate.
sentences.zh: 所以突然之间更多的女性在工作，这对外出出生率产生了影响。

sentences.en: So suddenly more women are working, which has an impact on the birth rate.
sentences.zh: 听起来好像男性工作减少了，或者虽然在工作但财务上没有安全感，所以他们不倾向于生孩子。

sentences.en: And then it sounds like men are not working as much or are working but are financially insecure, so they are not inclined to have children.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正当这一切发生时，有一件事没有改变，那就是这种根深蒂固的文化模式：当夫妻生了孩子后，

sentences.en: And as all of this is happening, there's one thing that isn't changing, and this is this very deeply entrenched cultural pattern that when couples do have children,
sentences.zh: 所有的家务都由女性来承担。

sentences.en: the women do all the work at home.
sentences.zh: 当你指的所有家务时。

sentences.en: And when you say all the work at home.
sentences.zh: 我是2016年夏天搬到日本的，我自己也是一个职场妈妈，我丈夫很好。

sentences.en: So I moved to Japan in the summer of 2016, and I'm a working mom myself, and my husband's great.
sentences.zh: 他会做晚饭，还会洗衣服。

sentences.en: He cooks dinner and he does laundry.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，就像任何有两个孩子的夫妇一样，我们有时会争论谁在做什么，谁做得更多。

sentences.en: But, of course, like any couple with two children, we sometimes argue about who's doing what and who's doing more.
sentences.zh: 但当我环顾四周时，我发现日本女性根本没法比。

sentences.en: But when I looked around, I noticed no comparison with Japanese women.
sentences.zh: 她们几乎包揽了一切。

sentences.en: They were pretty much doing everything.
sentences.zh: 不仅是包揽了所有的家务。

sentences.en: And it wasn't just that they were doing all the work at home.
sentences.zh: 而是社会对妈妈们应该做的事情的期望，远高于我在美国的职场妈妈经历过的任何事情。

sentences.en: It was that the expectations of what moms should do were much higher than anything that I had experienced as a working mom in the States.
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 比如，在日托中心，要求之一是父母（而且总是妈妈）必须写日志。

sentences.en: So, for example, at daycare, one of the things that's required is that the parents, and it's always the mom, has to keep a log.
sentences.zh: 每天早晨和每天晚上，她必须记录他们吃了什么、情绪如何、几点睡觉。

sentences.en: Every morning and every evening, she has to record what they ate, what their moods were, what time they went to sleep.
sentences.zh: 你每天都要在小本子上记下这些。

sentences.en: This is every day that you're putting this down in a little notebook.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这给妈妈增加了大量的额外劳动。

sentences.en: And that just seemed to me like a whole bunch of extra labor for the mom.
sentences.zh: 而且，不仅不是把沾满颜料和泥土的衣服带回家，

sentences.en: And then she's also, you know, instead of sending the kid an outfit that they might come home with paint splattered and dirt on it,
sentences.zh: 而是要给孩子准备三套衣服以便更换。

sentences.en: they're sending them three outfits so that they can change.
sentences.zh: 她们每个周末都要洗运动鞋。

sentences.en: They're washing their sneakers at the end of every week.
sentences.zh: 她们还要洗整套换洗的床单和毯子。

sentences.en: They're washing their, you know, whole set of change of sheets and blankets.
sentences.zh: 在日常漫步日本并观察所有公寓楼时，你会注意到的另一件事是，

sentences.en: The other thing that you notice when you're just walking around Japan and you look at all the apartment buildings,
sentences.zh: 如果你看阳台，每个人都在晾衣服。

sentences.en: if you look on the balconies, everybody's got laundry hanging out.
sentences.zh: 这是因为大多数中产阶级家庭甚至一些相当富裕的家庭都没有烘干机。

sentences.en: And that's because most middle-class families and even some fairly wealthy families don't have dryers.
sentences.zh: 所以，洗一炉衣服要多花很多力气。

sentences.en: So, that makes doing a load of laundry that much more work.
sentences.zh: 因此，有这么多的女性在夜间晾衣服。

sentences.en: And so, there are all these women that are hanging laundry at night.
sentences.zh: 因此，有这么多的女性在夜间晾衣服。

sentences.en: And as a reporting project, I sort of became obsessed with really diving into this.
sentences.zh: 作为一个纪实报道项目，我差不多有点痴迷于真正深入其中去探究。

sentences.en: What is it like to be a working mother in Japan?
sentences.zh: 在日本做一个职场母亲是怎样一种体验？

sentences.en: What specifically they were doing and why it was that they seemed so harried and overburdened.
sentences.zh: 她们具体在做些什么，为什么她们看起来总是那么忙碌和不堪重负。

sentences.en: And so, I spent a lot of time hanging out at daycare centers and talking to women as they came for pickup because it usually was mostly women.
sentences.zh: 因此，我花了很多时间在日托中心闲逛，在女性来接孩子时跟她们聊天，因为接孩子的通常大部分都是女性。

sentences.en: And then this one woman, Kazuko Yoshida, agreed to let us spend quite a lot of time with her.
sentences.zh: 后来，有一位名叫吉田和子的女士同意让我们花相当长的时间跟拍她。

sentences.en: So, one weekday, a photographer and I went to her apartment.
sentences.zh: 于是，在一个工作日，一位摄影师和我去了她的公寓。

sentences.en: We got there around 6.
sentences.zh: 我们大约6点到达那里。

sentences.en: And she and her husband are there with the two kids and they're getting ready for work.
sentences.zh: 她和丈夫以及两个孩子都在那里，他们正在为上班做准备。

sentences.en: But, you know, I notice little things, right?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我注意到了一些小细节，对吧？

sentences.en: He's sitting at the table with the kids and she's rushing around.
sentences.zh: 他正和孩子们坐在桌旁，而她则在四处忙碌。

sentences.en: Now, she's cooking the breakfast, she's clearing the table, she's packing their bags.
sentences.zh: 现在，她在做早餐，在收拾桌子，在打包他们的包。

sentences.en: And then it comes time to take them to daycare.
sentences.zh: 然后就到了带孩子们去日托中心的时候了。

sentences.en: And he says, okay, I'm going to take the kids to daycare.
sentences.zh: 接着他说，好吧，我要带孩子们去日托中心。

sentences.en: So, in my mind, that means he's going to take the kids to daycare on his own.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我的脑海里，这意味着他要独自带孩子们去日托中心。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: It turns out that he's going to accompany her to take the kids to daycare.
sentences.zh: 结果却是他要陪着她一起带孩子们去日托中心。

sentences.en: Why can't he do it himself?
sentences.zh: 为什么他不能自己去？

sentences.en: He just feels really anxious and insecure about it.
sentences.zh: 他对此感到非常焦虑和没有安全感。

sentences.en: And so, he said he just didn't feel that he could handle these two young children on his own.
sentences.zh: 所以，他说他觉得自己无法独自应付这两个年幼的孩子。

sentences.en: That he could help his wife, but he couldn't do it by himself.
sentences.zh: 他可以帮妻子的忙，但他不能一个人搞定。

sentences.en: You know, the youngest is baby, the older is a toddler, wrangling two kids.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，老小是个婴儿，大一点的是个幼儿，要应付两个孩子。

sentences.en: You know, it's a lot of work, I get it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这活儿很多，我懂。

sentences.en: But still, he just didn't think he could handle it.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，他还是觉得他应付不来。

sentences.en: And so, we accompanied Miss Yoshida to work.
sentences.zh: 于是，我们陪着吉田女士去上班。

sentences.en: She takes us into her office.
sentences.zh: 她带我们进入她的办公室。

sentences.en: She's a graphics designer.
sentences.zh: 她是一名平面设计师。

sentences.en: She lets us look around.
sentences.zh: 她让我们四处看看。

sentences.en: And then we say, you know what, we're going to come back and pick you up when you leave work so that we can go with you to pick up at daycare.
sentences.zh: 然后我们说，你知道吗，我们会在你下班时回来接你，这样我们就可以和你一起去日托中心接孩子了。

sentences.en: Because she's going to definitely do pick up because her husband's going to be working late.
sentences.zh: 因为她肯定得去接孩子，因为她丈夫要加班到很晚。

sentences.en: So, we get there to pick her up.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们赶到那里去接她。

sentences.en: We get to the station and we're about to get on the train to go pick up her kids.
sentences.zh: 我们到了车站，正准备上车去接她的孩子。

sentences.en: And she's like, let's let a train go by.
sentences.zh: 而她却说，让我们等这辆车开过去吧。

sentences.en: So, we let one train go by.
sentences.zh: 于是我们放过了一辆列车。

sentences.en: She's like, let's let another train go by.
sentences.zh: 她说，让另一辆列车也开过去吧。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: She said, this is the only time during the day that I have to myself.
sentences.zh: 她说，这是我一天当中唯一属于我自己的时间。

sentences.en: This is pretty intense.
sentences.zh: 这相当紧张压抑。

sentences.en: It is very intense.
sentences.zh: 确实非常紧张压抑。

sentences.en: And in fact, a lot of women who are still trying to decide what they want to do with their lives are looking at that model and saying, I'm not sure I want that.
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多仍在试图决定自己生活中想要什么的女性正在看着这种模式，并表示，我不知道我是否想要那样的生活。

sentences.en: There might be another way.
sentences.zh: 可能还有另一条出路。

sentences.en: And that other way means that a lot of women are either not getting married at all or even if they're getting married, they're not having children.
sentences.zh: 而那另一条出路意味着，许多女性要么根本不结婚，要么即使结了婚也不生孩子。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: They're basically opting out of motherhood because of the version of motherhood that they see in the culture.
sentences.zh: 由于她们在文化中看到的母亲形象，她们基本上选择不当母亲。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Montoko, you said that a big reason why Japanese women are opting out of motherhood is because so much of the burden of parenting falls on women.
sentences.zh: 蒙托科，你提到日本女性选择不当母亲的一个主要原因，是因为育儿的重担大多落在了女性身上。

sentences.en: So how widespread is this opting out phenomenon?
sentences.zh: 那么这种不愿生育的现象有多普遍呢？

sentences.en: So the proportion of women who've never been married is higher than it's ever been.
sentences.zh: 从未结过婚的女性比例比以往任何时候都要高。

sentences.en: And it's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 而且这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: I started to explore this partly because when I first came to Japan, every once in a while, my husband and I would go out on a Friday night.
sentences.zh: 我开始探讨这个问题，部分原因是当我刚来到日本时，每隔一段时间，我和丈夫会在周五晚上出去。

sentences.en: And we'd look around in the restaurants.
sentences.zh: 我们会环顾餐馆。

sentences.en: And everywhere we looked, it was all these groups of single women.
sentences.zh: 我们放眼望去，到处都是成群结队的单身女性。

sentences.en: And they look like they're really having a great time.
sentences.zh: 她们看起来玩得真的非常开心。

sentences.en: And there were no men around.
sentences.zh: 周围没有男人。

sentences.en: And I thought, okay, well, what's going on here?
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: It's not like you never see that in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说你在西方永远看不到这种情景。

sentences.en: But I just didn't see all that many couples.
sentences.zh: 但我就是没看到那么多情侣。

sentences.en: And it just seemed like there was this very segregated social life.
sentences.zh: 而且似乎存在着一种非常隔离的社交生活。

sentences.en: So I wanted to find out what was going on there.
sentences.zh: 所以我想弄清楚那里到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And as I started to talk to a lot of single women, it turned out that there's this whole kind of infrastructure
sentences.zh: 当我开始和许多单身女性交谈时，结果发现存在着这样一种完整的底层架构

sentences.en: that's growing around the fact that women have decided to opt out of marriage.
sentences.zh: 它围绕着女性决定不结婚这一事实而不断发展壮大。

sentences.en: They are working, so they have a good income.
sentences.zh: 她们在工作，所以她们有不错的收入。

sentences.en: There are these like solo karaoke bars or centers where they have women-only sections with these single booths where these women can go in and sing their hearts out.
sentences.zh: 有诸如单人卡拉OK酒吧或中心这样的地方，里面有女性专属区域和单人隔间，这些女性可以进去尽情歌唱。

sentences.en: There are these restaurants where they're for yakiniku, where women go and they're kind of grilling their own meat at their table.
sentences.zh: 有那种烤肉店，女性去那里，在自己的桌子上烤肉。

sentences.en: And that used to be kind of a thing that you would do.
sentences.zh: 这过去曾经是那种你会去做的事情。

sentences.en: You'd go sit at a group table.
sentences.zh: 你会去坐在一张集体桌旁。

sentences.en: But there are these restaurants now where they have these like solo booths for people to sit.
sentences.zh: 但现在有些餐馆设有供人们就座的单人隔间。

sentences.en: There are even like these photo studios where you can go get a wedding portrait taken.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有那种可以去拍结婚照的摄影工作室。

sentences.en: You know, you get dressed up in the wedding dress, but you're not getting married.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你穿上婚纱打扮起来，但你并不是要结婚。

sentences.en: It's called like a solo wedding photo.
sentences.zh: 这被称为单人婚纱照。

sentences.en: A solo wedding photo.
sentences.zh: 单人婚纱照。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a bit of an oxymoron, but I guess a celebration of a non-marriage.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点自相矛盾，但我想这是对非婚姻的一种庆祝。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There are women who are like, I love the dress.
sentences.zh: 有些女性会说，我喜欢这件衣服。

sentences.en: I love the idea of being celebrated.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢被庆祝的感觉。

sentences.en: I love the idea of looking more beautiful than I'll ever look.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢看起来比我任何时候都要美丽的感觉。

sentences.en: I want to memorialize my youth in this beautiful dress with this beautiful photo, but I don't need the actual wedding to do so.
sentences.zh: 我想用这件漂亮的衣服和这张漂亮的照片来纪念我的青春，但我不需要真正的婚礼来做到这一点。

sentences.en: So this phenomenon is so widespread that the culture is adjusting to women not wanting to be married.
sentences.zh: 所以这种现象如此普遍，以至于文化正在适应女性不想结婚的现状。

sentences.en: And, you know, in fairness, it's not necessarily that they're always saying, I don't want to be married, but they're making these choices.
sentences.zh: 而且，公平地说，这并不一定意味着她们总是说“我不想结婚”，而是她们正在做出这些选择。

sentences.en: They want to work.
sentences.zh: 她们想要工作。

sentences.en: They want to have a good time.
sentences.zh: 她们想要玩得开心。

sentences.en: They don't want to be trapped in these situations where they're at home all the time and not having fun, and that if they do have children, they're doing all the work.
sentences.zh: 她们不想被困在这样的境地里：整天待在家里却没有乐趣，而且如果她们生了孩子，所有的活都得她们干。

sentences.en: And so sometimes it's more tacit, it's more subliminal, but they are drifting away from these traditional family structures.
sentences.zh: 因此，有时这更隐蔽、更潜移默化，但她们确实在逐渐远离这些传统的家庭结构。

sentences.en: And I mentioned all of these unmarried women are, of course, not having that many children.
sentences.zh: 我提到所有这些未婚女性当然没有生那么多孩子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And it's pretty striking how many unmarried women there are now.
sentences.zh: 现在未婚女性的数量之多相当惊人。

sentences.en: So 20 years ago, if you looked at the cohort of women between the ages of 35 and 39, only 10% had never been married.
sentences.zh: 所以在20年前，如果你看看35岁到39岁之间的女性群体，只有10%的人从未结过婚。

sentences.en: And fast forward to today, that's nearly a quarter of those women have never been married.
sentences.zh: 快进到今天，这一比例接近这些女性的四分之一从未结过婚。

sentences.en: So more than double.
sentences.zh: 所以翻了一倍多。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: There are a lot of single women now.
sentences.zh: 现在有很多单身女性。

sentences.en: So in that prime childbearing phase of life, a full one quarter of Japanese women are unmarried and therefore unlikely to have children.
sentences.zh: 因此，在人生的那个黄金生育阶段，整整四分之一的日本女性未婚，因此不太可能生孩子。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What's interesting about the portrait you're painting is that up to a point, it resembles changes in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 你所描绘的现状有趣的地方在于，在某种程度上，它类似于西方的变革。

sentences.en: Women going to work, liking that work, making decisions based around the fact that they want to be co-equals in earning.
sentences.zh: 女性去工作，喜欢那份工作，并根据自己想要成为平等收入创造者的事实来做决定。

sentences.en: And yet that change in countries like the U.S.
sentences.zh: 然而，在美国这样的国家，这种变革

sentences.en: is accompanied by a kind of redistribution of parenting responsibilities and domestic work.
sentences.zh: 伴随着育儿责任和家务劳动的某种重新分配。

sentences.en: And it seems like Japan only had half the revolution.
sentences.zh: 而日本似乎只完成了半场革命。

sentences.en: The women go to work, but then things don't change at home the way they have in many parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 女性去工作了，但家里并没有像世界上许多地方那样发生改变。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So interestingly, women are working so much that the labor force participation rate among women in Japan is higher than it is even in the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以有趣的是，女性工作得如此努力，以至于日本女性的劳动力参与率甚至比美国还要高。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: And yet women are doing the vast majority of the work at home and the men are still doing so little.
sentences.zh: 然而，女性承担了家里绝大部分的工作，而男人们依然无所作为。

sentences.en: So check this statistic out.
sentences.zh: 所以来看看这个统计数据。

sentences.en: Men in Japan do on average 41 minutes a day of housework and childcare.
sentences.zh: 日本男性平均每天花41分钟做家务和照顾孩子。

sentences.en: And that compares to men in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，美国的男性

sentences.en: who are doing just under two and a half hours of housework and childcare a day.
sentences.zh: 每天花不到两个半小时做家务和照顾孩子。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So a very meaningful difference.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常巨大的差异。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And by the way, that figure for Japan is the lowest among the wealthiest countries in the world.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，日本的这个数字在世界上最富裕的国家中是最低的。

sentences.en: So in Japan right now, you have one of the highest workforce participations of women and lowest domestic participation from men.
sentences.zh: 所以目前在日本，你拥有极高的女性劳动力参与率和极低的男性家务参与率。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a huge disjunction.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个巨大的脱节。

sentences.en: You could probably say it's the biggest gap in the world.
sentences.zh: 你大概可以说这是世界上最大的差距。

sentences.en: So now that there is this phenomenon of women opting out of this gap that you have just described, not wanting to perpetuate it and therefore not have children,
sentences.zh: 所以，既然现在出现了女性选择不进入你刚刚描述的这个差距、不想将其延续下去从而不生孩子的现象，

sentences.en: what are the implications of this incredibly low birth rate that you have described?
sentences.zh: 你所描述的这种极其低迷的生育率会带来什么影响？

sentences.en: Well, one of the most obvious and biggest implications is that you suddenly have this society in which everyone is old.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最明显、最大的影响之一就是，你突然拥有了一个所有人都在变老的社会。

sentences.en: According to the United Nations, its population is the oldest in the world.
sentences.zh: 根据联合国的统计，它的人口是世界上老龄化最严重的。

sentences.en: There was a time when it looked like Japan would become the number one economic power in the world.
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，日本似乎将成为世界第一大经济强国。

sentences.en: Under a million babies born just last year.
sentences.zh: 就在去年，出生的婴儿不到一百万。

sentences.en: And when you have fewer people being born...
sentences.zh: 当出生的人口变少时……

sentences.en: And you do not have consumption.
sentences.zh: 而你又没有消费。

sentences.en: And old people do not consume.
sentences.zh: 老年人是不消费的。

sentences.en: You have fewer people growing up to become workers.
sentences.zh: 长大后成为劳动者的人数就会减少。

sentences.en: And that means you have fewer people contributing to the social security system that you need to sustain this growing population of old people.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，为维持日益庞大的老年人口所需的社会保障体系做出贡献的人变少了。

sentences.en: The benefits are going to the elder generation, whereas the burden is borne by the working and young generation.
sentences.zh: 福利流向了老年一代，而负担却由工作和年轻一代承担。

sentences.en: And you also have fewer people to become doctors and nurses and home health aides, caregivers.
sentences.zh: 而且你也没有足够的人来成为医生、护士、家庭保健员和看护人员。

sentences.en: As the elderly population increases, more staff are required to treat them.
sentences.zh: 随着老年人口的增加，需要更多的医护人员来治疗他们。

sentences.en: This is creating a growing financial burden for hospitals.
sentences.zh: 这给医院带来了日益沉重的财务负担。

sentences.en: And is that showing up in the Japanese economy?
sentences.zh: 这在日元经济中显现出来了吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对显现出来了。

sentences.en: Japanese employers are desperate for workers, particularly in areas that are very labor-intensive.
sentences.zh: 日本雇主极其渴望工人，特别是在劳动密集型领域。

sentences.en: So given that this demographic problem, this low birth rate, is now understood to be causing this economic problem in Japan, what is Japan doing about it?
sentences.zh: 鉴于这一人口问题、低生育率现在被认为正在日本造成这种经济问题，日本对此采取了什么措施？

sentences.en: So a couple things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有几件事。

sentences.en: One is that after years and years of resisting, Japan is slowly starting to open its borders and allow non-Japanese people to move here, but in a pretty limited way.
sentences.zh: 一是经过长年累月的抵制，日本正慢慢开始打开国门，允许非日本人搬到这里来，但方式相当有限。

sentences.en: So a couple of years ago...
sentences.zh: 所以几年前……

sentences.en: Japan's parliament has passed a new law.
sentences.zh: 日本国会通过了一项新法律。

sentences.en: Parliament passed a law.
sentences.zh: 国会通过了一项法律。

sentences.en: Opening the door to nearly 350,000 foreign workers in a country where immigration has long been taboo.
sentences.zh: 在一个长期将移民视为禁忌的国家，向近35万外国劳工打开了大门。

sentences.en: That allowed a new category of visas for people from other countries to come in and work.
sentences.zh: 这为来自其他国家的人员入境工作开辟了一个新的签证类别。

sentences.en: Both blue-collar and skilled workers will be allowed in under different schemes.
sentences.zh: 根据不同的计划，蓝领工人和技术工人将被允许入境。

sentences.en: And the conditions for coming in were pretty stark.
sentences.zh: 而且进入的条件非常严苛。

sentences.en: So people who get these visas can only stay for five years.
sentences.zh: 所以获得这些签证的人只能停留五年。

sentences.en: They're not allowed to bring their families.
sentences.zh: 他们不允许把家人带过来。

sentences.en: There's a pretty high bar that they have to learn to speak Japanese.
sentences.zh: 他们必须学会说日语，这个门槛相当高。

sentences.en: So I think it's going to be quite difficult for them to attract a lot of people to take these jobs.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他们要吸引大量人员来做这些工作将会相当困难。

sentences.en: And even if they do, they're only issuing 350,000 visas over five years, which is kind of a drop in the bucket for the need.
sentences.zh: 即便他们做到了，五年内也只发放三十五万个签证，对于需求来说简直是杯水车薪。

sentences.en: Just to be sure I understand this, despite having a population crisis, Japan is letting immigrants in, but they cannot bring their families,
sentences.zh: 为了确保我没理解错，尽管面临人口危机，日本还是允许移民入境，但他们不能带家属，

sentences.en: who I imagine would help them procreate?
sentences.zh: 我想象中这些家属本可以帮他们繁衍后代？

sentences.en: That's how inhospitable Japan is to people who aren't Japanese.
sentences.zh: 这就是日本对非日本人的排外程度。

sentences.en: I think it's sort of a fear-based idea that we don't want people to put down roots here.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种基于恐惧的想法，我们不想让人们在这里扎根。

sentences.en: Former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe would not use the word immigration, and he often would say this is not an immigration policy.
sentences.zh: 前首相安倍晋三不愿使用“移民”这个词，他经常说这不是一项移民政策。

sentences.en: It's a foreign worker policy.
sentences.zh: 这是一项外国工人政策。

sentences.en: So I think it was designed specifically to allay fears that Japan would become a nation of immigrants, which is something that I wouldn't say a majority,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为它的设计专门是为了消除人们对日本将成为一个移民国家的恐惧，我不敢说是大多数人，

sentences.en: but certainly a very large and vocal segment of the population does not want.
sentences.zh: 但肯定有很大一部分且声音很大的群体是不希望这样的。

sentences.en: And then the other solution to the economic problem, sort of ironically, is this notion of getting more women to go to work.
sentences.zh: 然后解决经济问题的另一个办法，有点讽刺的是，就是让更多女性去工作的这种理念。

sentences.en: When Prime Minister Abe came into office, he said one of the things he wanted to do to pull the economy out of a long period of stagnation was to push and empower women.
sentences.zh: 当安倍首相上台时，他说他想把经济从长期萧条中拉出来，想要做的事情之一就是推动和赋能女性。

sentences.en: And so he called this policy Womanomics.
sentences.zh: 于是他把这项政策称为“女性经济学”。

sentences.en: It's an idea that's known as Womanomics.
sentences.zh: 这是一个被称为“女性经济学”的想法。

sentences.en: Womanomics is the name for Abe's policy to close Japan's gender gap.
sentences.zh: 女性经济学是安倍旨在缩小日本性别差距的政策名称。

sentences.en: An ambitious plan to boost the number of female managers by 30 percent in four years.
sentences.zh: 一项雄心勃勃的计划：在四年内将女性管理人员的数量提高百分之三十。

sentences.en: And the idea is if more women are working, you have this sort of untapped pool of highly educated, talented, native-born workers here in Japan.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是，如果有更多女性在工作，在日本这里，你就拥有了一批未被充分利用的、受过良好教育的、有才华的本土劳动力资源。

sentences.en: And so he was saying we need more women to go to work.
sentences.zh: 因此他一直在说我们需要让更多的女性去工作。

sentences.en: But, of course, the problem with that, as we've seen, is that when the women go to work,
sentences.zh: 但是，正如我们所看到的，这其中存在的问题是，当女性去工作时，

sentences.en: they either decide that they like working so much that they don't want to get married and have children.
sentences.zh: 她们要么觉得工作太开心了，以至于不想结婚生子。

sentences.en: Or if they're working and they also have children, it's so difficult to combine the two that it's certainly not an incentive to have a lot of children.
sentences.zh: 要么就是如果她们一边工作一边还要带孩子，要将这两者兼顾是如此困难，这绝对无法激励人们生很多孩子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So neither of the programs that you have just identified would seem to do almost anything to increase the birth rate.
sentences.zh: 因此，你刚才指出的这两项计划似乎几乎都无法起到提高生育率的作用。

sentences.en: It might temporarily improve the economy.
sentences.zh: 它可能会暂时改善经济。

sentences.en: But if the long-term problem in Japan is that not enough babies are being born, neither of these things is going to do all that much to change that.
sentences.zh: 但如果日本的长期问题是没有足够的新生儿出生，这两项措施都无法对此做出太大改变。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the thing that would really change things is a dramatic shift in the culture.
sentences.zh: 所以真正能改变现状的是文化的巨大转变。

sentences.en: And we're starting to see really tiny baby steps.
sentences.zh: 而我们开始看到非常微小的婴儿般的步伐。

sentences.en: Sometimes on the weekend, you'll see dads at the playground with their kids.
sentences.zh: 有时在周末，你会看到爸爸们带着孩子在游乐场玩耍。

sentences.en: You hear of fathers that are learning to cook, do more housework.
sentences.zh: 你听说有些父亲正在学习做饭、做更多家务。

sentences.en: And then you have this politician.
sentences.zh: 然后你有了这位政治家。

sentences.en: He's actually the son of a former prime minister who was pretty famous, well-known friend of George Bush, Junichiro Koizumi, his son Shinjiro Koizumi,
sentences.zh: 他其实是一位前首相的儿子，那位前首相相当有名，是乔治·布什众所周知的朋友小泉纯一郎，他的儿子就是小泉进次郎，

sentences.en: who's now the environment minister.
sentences.zh: 他现在是环境大臣。

sentences.en: His wife was pregnant when they got married.
sentences.zh: 他们结婚时他的妻子已经怀孕了。

sentences.en: And he announced right before the baby was born that he was going to take paternity leave.
sentences.zh: 他在孩子出生前夕宣布他要休陪产假。

sentences.en: But when he first announced that he was considering taking paternity leave, believe it or not, he got a lot of blowback.
sentences.zh: 但当他最初宣布考虑休陪产假时，信不信由你，他遭到了很大的反对。

sentences.en: So there were some conservative politicians who said, you know, this is a sign that he's not very serious about his job.
sentences.zh: 所以有一些保守派政客说，你知道，这表明他对工作不够认真。

sentences.en: And on social media, people were criticizing him for even daring to suggest that he might take paternity leave.
sentences.zh: 而在社交媒体上，人们批评他甚至敢于暗示自己可能会休陪产假。

sentences.en: How dare he?
sentences.zh: 他怎么敢？

sentences.en: That kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: So it took him a while to actually firmly announce that he definitely was planning to do it.
sentences.zh: 因此，他花了点时间才真正坚定地宣布他确实有这个计划。

sentences.en: And then when the baby was born, here's what he did.
sentences.zh: 然后当孩子出生时，他是这么做的。

sentences.en: He took two weeks over a course of three months.
sentences.zh: 他在三个月的时间里休了两周假。

sentences.en: And he said he was going to be kind of telecommuting for part of that.
sentences.zh: 他说他在那期间的一部分时间里会进行远程办公。

sentences.en: So this was definitely paternity leave light.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是简易版的陪产假。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, a significant gesture.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个很有意义的姿态。

sentences.en: But like you said, paternity leave light.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，是简易版陪产假。

sentences.en: And what did that episode tell you?
sentences.zh: 那集节目说明了什么？

sentences.en: Well, on the one hand, it feels like there's an effort to try, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，一方面，感觉确实有人在努力尝试，对吧？

sentences.en: His father certainly didn't take paternity leave.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲肯定没有休过陪产假。

sentences.en: There was never any question that he would take leave when his children were born.
sentences.zh: 当他的孩子出生时，他根本不可能考虑休假。

sentences.en: So the fact that his son, a prominent politician, he's mooted as potentially being a future prime minister,
sentences.zh: 所以，他的儿子——一位杰出的政治家，被视为未来首相的潜在人选——

sentences.en: had decided that he would stake some of his political capital to take paternity leave is definitely a gesture of people trying to change the culture.
sentences.zh: 决定冒着消耗政治资本的风险去休陪产假，这绝对是一种试图改变文化的姿态。

sentences.en: On the other hand, the blowback that he got, the fact that he had to make a big deal of just taking two weeks off,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，他遭到的强烈反对，他仅仅休假两周就得大肆宣扬一番，

sentences.en: shows how difficult it is to change this really entrenched culture of what roles men and what roles women are supposed to play.
sentences.zh: 这表明要改变这种根深蒂固的关于男女应扮演什么角色的文化是多么困难。

sentences.en: Matoko, I'm curious.
sentences.zh: 马德子，我很想知道。

sentences.en: What do you expect to happen to that town, now filled with more dolls than people, that you started our conversation describing?
sentences.zh: 你在一开始交谈时描述的那个现在玩偶比人还多的城镇，你认为它会发生什么变化？

sentences.en: I think it's going to disappear.
sentences.zh: 我认为它会消失。

sentences.en: I mean, there are only two dozen people left.
sentences.zh: 我是说，只剩下二十四个人了。

sentences.en: There's nobody of childbearing age left, so nobody's going to be having any more kids.
sentences.zh: 已经没有育龄人口了，所以不会再有人生孩子了。

sentences.en: And they're all pretty old.
sentences.zh: 而且他们年纪都挺大了。

sentences.en: So as they die off, the town will die off.
sentences.zh: 所以随着他们相继离世，小镇也将消亡。

sentences.en: And the only people left will be the dolls.
sentences.zh: 剩下的只有那些玩偶了。

sentences.en: Matoko, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 马德子，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: The new prime minister of Japan, Yoshihide Suga, has said that raising the country's birth rate is a major priority
sentences.zh: 日本新首相菅义伟表示，提高国家的出生率是重中之重，

sentences.en: and has pledged to make the country's national insurance system pay for fertility treatments to encourage families to have more children.
sentences.zh: 并承诺让国家国民健康保险系统支付不孕不育治疗费用，以鼓励家庭多生孩子。

sentences.en: Japan's government now projects that unless the birth rate changes, the country's population, which now stands at 126 million, will fall below 100 million by 2053
sentences.zh: 日本政府目前预测，除非出生率发生变化，否则该国目前为1.26亿的人口将在2053年跌至1亿以下，

sentences.en: and fall to 88 million by 2065.
sentences.zh: 并在2065年跌至8800万。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, Pfizer, whose COVID-19 vaccine is expected to be authorized in the coming days for adolescents between 12 and 15, said it would seek authorization to give the vaccine
sentences.zh: 周二，辉瑞公司表示，其新冠疫苗预计将在未来几天内获批用于12至15岁的青少年，

sentences.en: to children between the ages of 2 and 11 later this fall.
sentences.zh: 该公司将在今年秋季稍晚时寻求批准将该疫苗用于2至11岁的儿童。

sentences.en: So far, the FDA has authorized Pfizer's vaccine under a temporary emergency order and has yet to grant the vaccine full approval.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，美国食品药品监督管理局是在临时紧急授权下批准辉瑞疫苗的，尚未授予该疫苗完全批准。

sentences.en: During a call with investors, Pfizer said it would soon seek such approval from the government.
sentences.zh: 在与投资者的电话会议上，辉瑞表示很快将向政府寻求这种批准。

sentences.en: Full approval would allow Pfizer to market its vaccine directly to consumers and could make it easier for companies, schools, and government agencies
sentences.zh: 完全批准将允许辉瑞直接向消费者营销其疫苗，并可能使公司、学校和政府机构更容易

sentences.en: to require that workers be vaccinated before returning to work in person.
sentences.zh: 要求工人在返回实体工作场所之前接种疫苗。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Bianca Gaver, Adiza Egan, Kelly Prime, and Alexandra Lee Young.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由比安卡·加弗、阿迪扎·埃甘、凯利·普莱姆和亚历山德拉·李·杨制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow and engineered by Chris Ward.
sentences.zh: 丽莎·周剪辑，克里斯·沃德混音。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是本期《The Daily》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《The Wirecutter Show》节目中，我们正为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人们宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是全黑睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是为了睡觉而昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症、食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何平台上收听《The Wirecutter Show》。
